chunks: A number of our companions, from Sahl ibn Ziyad and Ahmad ibn Muhammad, altogether from Al-Hasan ibn Mahboub, from Umar ibn Yazeed, who said:

Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him) said: 'Al-Ma'ruf (acts of kindness/goodness) is something besides the Zakat, so draw closer to Allah, Mighty and Majestic, through righteousness and maintaining ties of kinship.'

key_terms.الْمَعْرُوفُ: Acts of kindness, goodness, or customary charity

ai.seo_question: What is the difference between Ma'ruf and Zakat in Shia hadith?
ai.summary: In this hadith from *Al-Kafi*, Imam al-Sadiq (peace be upon him) clarifies that 'Al-Ma'ruf' encompasses voluntary righteous deeds distinct from the obligatory 'Zakat', thereby encouraging believers to expand their spiritual practice beyond legal minimums. He specifically highlights 'Silat al-Rahim' (maintaining kinship ties) as a primary means of drawing closer to Allah, reflecting the Shia emphasis on family bonds as a core component of faith and social cohesion.
